purpose: Candidate chat, coding, retrieval and tool-use acceptance. No GPU or network execution is authorized by this menu.

execution.path: lib/workstation/assistant_acceptance.py against one named boundary per run: fixture, direct (native SGLang), gateway (authenticated boundary), webui-api (Open WebUI API). Browser UI and coding-client sessions use the recorded scenario checklists.
execution.token_accounting: Use the candidate tokenizer and chat template, including tool definitions, history, output allowance and measured scheduler reserve. Do not estimate tokens from characters.
execution.privacy: Use synthetic fixtures. Public search queries must not contain private project passages.
execution.acceptance: Every required deterministic check must pass in every repetition. Retain failures. Coding requires real tests in the existing isolated owner workflow; citations require source support. Do not treat transport fixtures or an LLM self-score as model qualification. An unreachable boundary is NOT RUN, never PASS.
execution.repetitions_note: Unique tasks and repetitions are counted separately; a repetition never counts as another task.

cases.prompt: Return exactly one JSON object with keys status and count. Set status to ready and count to 3. Include no prose or Markdown.
Fix this Python function so it returns only integers, excluding booleans, in original order: def integers(values): return [v for v in values if isinstance(v, int)]. Return the corrected function.

grading.execution: Inspect the response, then use the existing isolated owner execution workflow. Never execute model-generated code in the planner.

cases.prompt: The tests in test_windows.py fail. Fix the bug in windows.py so all tests pass. Return each changed file in full in one fenced block whose info string is the file path, for example ```path/to/file```. Change nothing else.

go test fails for this package. Fix retry.go so the documented behaviour and the tests agree. Return each changed file in full in one fenced block whose info string is the file path, for example ```path/to/file```. Change nothing else.

terraform validate fails for this module under the pinned Terraform 1.7 range. Make the smallest compatible fix. Return each changed file in full in one fenced block whose info string is the file path, for example ```path/to/file```. Change nothing else.

This playbook fails ansible-playbook --syntax-check on ansible-core 2.19. Make it compatible without changing behaviour. Return each changed file in full in one fenced block whose info string is the file path, for example ```path/to/file```. Change nothing else.

Supplied evidence (synthetic):
[E1] kubectl get pod api-7c9 -o wide: STATUS CrashLoopBackOff, RESTARTS 6
[E2] kubectl describe pod api-7c9: Last State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled, Exit Code: 137; Limits: memory 512Mi
[E3] container log (previous): 'loaded 4 cache shards; resident 498Mi'
[E4] deployment api: env CACHE_SHARDS=4 (changed from 2 at 09:12 UTC)
Return only JSON with keys root_cause (one of OOMKilled, ImagePullBackOff, ProbeFailure, ConfigError), container_limit, trigger_env (the name of the environment variable whose change triggered it), evidence (list of evidence IDs that support the cause).
rubric: Explains that the shard count change raised resident memory to the limit
Proposes reverting CACHE_SHARDS or raising the limit with capacity evidence
Does not recommend deleting the pod or namespace as a fix

steps: Open a disposable copy of the fixture as the workspace
Ask the client to run the tests, read the failure, edit windows.py and rerun the tests
Interrupt the session after the first edit, resume it, and confirm the edit and test state are retained
Force context compaction with a long prior turn, then ask for the test status and confirm it is still correct
checks: tests pass in the network-free sandbox
client log shows a failing then passing test run
post-compaction answer matches the actual test status

final answer cites the supplied URL
